svg.title: Dynamic Regime GNN final project poster
svg.desc: Heterogeneous GNN with Bloomberg supplier/customer/holder edges outperforms ablations on cross-sectional S&P 500 return rank prediction with statistical significance.

g.text: A statistically rigorous evaluation of supplier, customer, and institutional-holder graph structure.
Srotriyo Sengupta and Yifan Zhang · ECE 538 Final Project
Bloomberg-augmented heterogeneous GNN significantly outperforms every alternative on cross-sectional 5-day rank prediction.
Effect is specific to real economic edges.
Random/sector proxy graphs are statistically indistinguishable from no-graph at all.
The original regime-classification target is defined by percentile
rules on aggregate market features. Logistic regression on those
same features hits AUC ≈ 0.96 — exposing label leakage that
prevents the GNN from demonstrating its value.
For each day t and stock i, label = rank-quantile of
forward 5-day return across all stocks on day t.
1.04 M parameters · per-relation scaled-dot-product attention · class-weighted CE · AdamW + cosine LR
Price/volume + Top Suppliers, Top Customers, Top 20 Holders
per ticker. Workbook is proprietary — not redistributable.
Validation: held-out 2022Q4–2024 (covers 2022 crash, SVB, Aug 2024 carry unwind).
Per-date macro-F1 on val split (best epoch, mean ± std of 5 seeds).
Three non-Bloomberg configs are statistically indistinguishable from each other (all paired t-tests n.s.).
Isolating each Bloomberg edge type (n=3 seeds, ±std).
Supply-only reproduces 96% of the gain (p < .01 vs No-graph)
Holder Jaccard is dominated by universal owners (Vanguard, BlackRock) — harmful alone, marginally helpful combined.
Bloomberg vs No-graph at three train cutoffs (n=3 seeds each).
Δ macro-F1: +0.015 to +0.021 across all three windows
Real Bloomberg edges > every ablation (p < .001 vs No-graph).
Supplier/customer edges alone reproduce 96% of the gain.
Effect direction stable across 3 walk-forward train cutoffs.
Class-weighted CE; AdamW + cosine LR; gradient clipping.
